aesthetic: The Circulating-Library Set — a triple-decker read to a borrower's ledger
anchor: A Mudie's Select Library three-volume 'triple-decker' set in publisher's cloth, read through the subscriber's reading-schedule ledger and pencil marginalia: Carlyle's 1837 Fraser edition is itself three volumes (The Bastille / The Constitution / The Guillotine), 20 books, 159 chapters, and this primer's whole job is to pace a first-time borrower through them in six weeks.
rationale: The sibling corpus (The Burnt Manuscript) reads the book as a fire: ember, Caslon, warm char. This corpus reads the book as an object you check out and finish: three volumes to be borrowed one at a time, a ruled ledger of weeks, a numbered tick-list of ten chapters. So the world is cool and bookish rather than incandescent: library-cloth teal-green, the plum of a borrower's ticket, Prussian-blue ledger ink, ochre catalogue-card edge, pencil-graphite slate for marginalia, on pale sage ledger paper. Display type is a humanist sans (the stamped spine-label and ticket), body is Georgia, so nothing here shares the sibling's Caslon serif voice.

fonts.body: Georgia, 'Iowan Old Style', 'Times New Roman', serif
